security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan RTL, when the PDIS sample record hardware writes the address validity indicator to pdisadr1[63] or pdisadr2[63] (old spec behavior) instead of setting the dedicated ADR1V/ADR2V bits in pdishdrev at bits [33:32] (new spec: 'bits 1 name ADR1V' and 'bits 1 name ADR2V' inserted between HPM[31:3] and FLUSHED), the validity information lands in the wrong bit position. Additionally, if the physical address in pdisadr2 is written without the mandatory right-shift-by-2 encoding (to accommodate PA > XLEN, e.g., Sv32 34-bit PA on RV32), the reported physical address is corrupted by a factor of 4 and privilege-mode-dependent address bits may be exposed in the upper bits.
security_spec.summary: Address validity moved from pdisadr[63] to dedicated ADR1V/ADR2V fields in pdishdrev; physical addresses in pdisadr2 must be right-shifted by 2 to accommodate PA > XLEN — mismatched bit positions cause stale/invalid addresses to leak and physical address corruption
